newsitem.title: UK: W. African crude quiet ahead of Nigeria prices.
newsitem.headline: W. African crude quiet ahead of Nigeria prices.

text.p: The West African crude market was quietly steady with Asian buyers taking a breather on Tuesday ahead of the publication of Nigerian prices for July, which are expected this week, traders said.
South Korean buyers who have helped brake a slide in West African prices in the past two weeks were looking relaxed and had not entered the market in force so far this week, they said.
But Asians were expected to break the buying lull later in the month for cargoes loading second half July.
"Everything is quiet before the NNPC prices," a trader said.
"The eastern demand has stopped, and that has been the only thing stopping the market from falling further. It needs Northwest European, Mediterranean and U.S. demand to lift it higher," he said.
Traders said two Brass Rivers were heard done but values were not known. An Escravos was done at Dated Brent +22 cents but some traders saw the value as on the low side.
West African grades have slid around 15 cents across the board in the past two weeks amid a glut of unsold material, with light grades suffering slightly more than gas oil grades.
Bonny Light is assessed at around Dated +30/35, Qua Iboe at around Dated +25 and Brass River at around Dated -42/-37 cents or around five cents over Bonny.
Pennington is seen by one trader at around Dated +80 cents, while traders assess Forcados at around Dated +10. Rabi is seen at around dated +10, with Polanca at +20.
On the Mediterranean market, Urals continues quiet and assessed at Dated -$1.10/-$1.15.

Traders continue to wait word from Syrian state oil company Sytrol on pricing for July. One said it appeared Sytrol was holding back a final decision in order to wait for the Urals market to settle at a higher number.
Some believe Urals will firm in the event that delays occur in preparations for a resumption of exports of Iraq's Kirkuk sour under the second six-month phase of the U.N. "oil-for-food" programme.
